[02:41] Carlos: sure. there are two main levers: continuous batching (combining requests in the runtime) and KV cache / prefix caching. batching increases throughput and reduces per-token compute overhead; caching avoids re-computing prefixes entirely for repeated prompts. in practice, for a chat or templated prompt workload we often see 20-60% lower tokens billed effectively when cache hits are high. but batching can increase tail latency if not tuned, so tradeoffs exist.

[04:05] Jordan: what about quantization — can we run int8 or other quantized models on dedicated to reduce cost? any quality regression risks?

[04:12] Carlos: yes, we support int8 and 4-bit quantization profiles. we provide model-quality/regression tests with your eval set to benchmark quality. typical trading prompt small seqs often tolerate int8 well, but we always recommend rolling a canary and running evals. quantization plus batching often moves unit cost substantially.
